samples.summary: DOCX `w:color`/`w:shd@w:fill` still emit non-hex color strings verbatim — escaping fixes well-formedness but not schema validity
samples.evidence: Line 77-85 now escape the resolved color, and the comment explicitly acknowledges that `InlineStyle.color` "really can hold a non-palette string (DOCX/PPTX import…)". But `escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))` still emits whatever string arrived. `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:150-155` copies pasted HTML CSS straight into `style.color` / `style.backgroundColor`, and browsers normalize those to `rgb(255, 0, 0)` / `rgba(…)`. Exporting such a doc produces `<w:color w:val="rgb(255, 0, 0)"/>`, which is not an `ST_HexColor` (6 hex digits or `auto`) — Word typically flags the part as unreadable content rather than rendering the color. The change touched exactly these two lines and hardened only the injection axis; a `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/` (or CSS-color→hex normalization) check before emitting would make the attribute valid and would make `escapeXmlAttr` unnecessary here.

samples.summary: `renderListMarker` treats a cleared marker color ('') as *set*, discarding the inline's real color
samples.evidence: `const colorSource = m?.color ?? firstInline?.color;` — `??` only falls through on null/undefined, so `marker.color === ''` (the legacy issue-#728 reset the rest of this diff is normalizing away) wins over a legitimate `firstInline.color`. The subsequent `resolveStoredColor` then maps '' → undefined → `theme.defaultColor`, so a marker whose color was cleared silently ignores the inline color it used to inherit. The new test at packages/docs/test/view/render-list-marker.test.ts ("paints an empty-string marker color with the theme default" with `inline: { color: '#FF9900' }`) locks this in. If '' means "unset" everywhere else in this change, the `??` chain should normalize it too (e.g. `(m?.color || undefined) ?? (firstInline?.color)`).

samples.summary: Cleared link color no longer falls back to the blue hyperlink default under a theme-aware resolver
samples.evidence: `const resolvedColor = resolveStoredColor(resolveColor, style.color);` then `if (style.href) { if (!resolvedColor) textColor = '#1155cc'; }`. Previously `resolveColor('')` under slides' `makeColorResolver` returned '' → `|| undefined` → falsy → the link painted blue. After the change '' is normalized before the resolver, so `makeColorResolver` returns the deck's `text` role color (truthy) and the hyperlink loses its blue default. The behavior may be intended (cleared ⇒ theme), but it is a silent rendering change for links in slides text boxes and is not covered by any of the new tests.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: docx-style-map.ts:77-85 emits `w:color w:val` and `w:shd w:fill` from `defaultColorResolver(...)` with only `.replace('#','')` and XML escaping — no ST_HexColor shape check. `model/color.ts:14-22` is a pure pass-through for string and srgb forms, so it is not a guard. The ingress is real and unmitigated: clipboard.ts:150-155 copies `el.style.color`/`backgroundColor` verbatim (browsers normalize these to `rgb(...)`/`rgba(...)`), reached on paste via text-editor.ts:1117; I grepped `sanitiz|normaliz|migrat` across packages/docs/src and the only style normalizer (normalizeBlockStyle, model/types.ts:272) does not touch inline colors. backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:192 and docs-tree.spec.ts:143 confirm `rgb(255, 128, 0)` values persist in the tree. No downstream rescue: docx-exporter.ts:217 passes inline.style straight through, and the only hex validation in the package (pdf-style-map.ts:146) is on the PDF path; `cssColorToHex` exists only in packages/sheets and is not imported by docs. Existing tests at test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:79-87 affirmatively codify emitting non-hex strings verbatim (escaped), so the guard demonstrably does not exist. Blocking as a correctness/output-validity defect (not the injection axis): an ordinary paste-then-export flow produces a DOCX attribute violating ST_HexColor, causing Word to flag unreadable content or silently drop the color — broken core export flow, major.

finding.summary: Collapsing '' to `undefined` after the resolver bypasses theme-aware fallback, painting legacy cleared runs in the docs default color on themed slides
finding.evidence: `const resolvedColor = resolveColor(style.color) || undefined;` then `let textColor = resolvedColor ?? theme.defaultColor;`. For slides the injected resolver (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52-63 `makeColorResolver`) maps a *missing* color to the deck theme's text color (`themeText`), but a legacy `''` reaches the resolver, comes back `''`, and is turned into the docs `theme.defaultColor` (near-black) instead of being re-resolved as "no color" through the theme. On a dark deck theme, runs whose color was cleared before this fix paint dark-on-dark (effectively invisible) rather than in the theme text color. The correct handling is to fall back to `resolveColor(undefined)`. The same shape appears at renderListMarker (paint-layout.ts:558, `resolveColor(colorSource) || theme.defaultColor`) and in resolveColorAtPosition (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:75/80, `|| fallback` where the slides caller passes the docs `Theme.cursorColor`, text-box-editor.ts:578-583), so the caret over such a run also reverts to the docs cursor color on a dark slide.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. paint-layout.ts:388 is `const resolvedColor = resolveStoredColor(resolveColor, style.color);`, not `resolveColor(style.color) || undefined`. resolveStoredColor (color.ts:45-50) normalizes '' to undefined BEFORE calling the resolver: `resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined`, so a legacy cleared run hits slides' makeColorResolver `if (c == null) return themeText;` branch (text-renderer.ts:54-55) and paints the deck theme text color — exactly the "correct handling" the finding says is missing. The trailing `|| undefined` only guards a resolver that itself returns ''. Same for renderListMarker (paint-layout.ts:555, `resolveStoredColor(resolveColor, colorSource) ?? theme.defaultColor`) and for the caret path (color.ts:103/108 `resolveStoredColor(colorResolver, ...) ?? fallback`, consumed by text-box-editor.ts:578-583); the finding's cited color.ts:75/80 are wrapLegacyColor/storedColorsEqual, not the fallback lines. No path exists where '' reaches a theme-aware resolver unnormalized.
